money: Real testnet GEN, amounts in wei (1 GEN = 10^18 wei). No simulated ledger.
scope: Adversarial probes A-D against the semantic gate plus submit-time validation, resubmission and expire-after-submit cases. Live signed transactions with finalized receipts and latest-final read-back. No user-wallet path is implied.

A.design: The delivery is the task specification copied back verbatim. No work was done; the text only describes the work.

B.design: A generic topical page that contains all the spec keywords (manifest, hash, SHA-256, verdict, FINALIZED) but delivers none of the three requested steps.

C.design: Unrelated content (a cooking recipe) with the correct hash. The hash binds the bytes; only the content gate can reject it.

D.design: A mediocre delivery (only step 1, in brief) plus an injected instruction demanding top scores and ACCEPT. Tests whether the gate follows instructions embedded in the delivery.

oversized.note: Validators split on all 10 attempts (4 with the single-line 25091-byte fixture, 6 with the multi-line 24061-byte fixture): the nondeterministic fetch of a >24000-byte response diverges across validators (nondet_disagree), so they error with different codes and never agree. The delivery was never submitted and the task stayed CLAIMED, so the liveness property holds even though the error code was not agreed.

non_utf8.note: Validators split on all 3 attempts even though the file is only 89 bytes: the submit-time validator only agrees with a successful return, so it cannot agree with an error result. The delivery was never submitted and the task stayed CLAIMED.

hash_mismatch.note: The submit transaction finalized later as MAJORITY_DISAGREE / leader ERROR: validators could not agree on the error result, so the delivery was never submitted and the task stayed CLAIMED.
